title: Prime-torsion coefficient reduction for the punctual tensor comparison
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $S'$ be $K$-schemes and let $g:T\to S'$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism. Put $X'=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $p:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $n\ge1$ be invertible in $K$, set $R=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, and let $\ell\mid n$ be prime. Let $\mathcal E$ be a flat $R$-module sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and let $\mathcal F$ be an $R$-module sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ with $\ell\mathcal F=0$, regarded also as a sheaf of $\mathbf F_\ell$-vector spaces through $R\to\mathbf F_\ell$. Write $k=\mathbf F_\ell$, $\overline{\mathcal E}=\mathcal E/\ell\mathcal E$, and $U_V:D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},k)\to D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ for termwise restriction of scalars along $R\to k$. Then $\overline{\mathcal E}$ is flat over $k$, and there are natural isomorphisms
$$p^{-1}\mathcal E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_{*,R}\mathcal F\cong U_{X'}\bigl(p^{-1}\overline{\mathcal E}\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_{*,k}\mathcal F\bigr),$$
$$Rh_{*,R}\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}\mathcal E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)\cong U_{X'}Rh_{*,k}\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}\overline{\mathcal E}\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr).$$
Here all sheaves are on small etale sites, the derived categories are those of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], tensor is [def-kun-derived-tensor], and direct and inverse images, with counit $\varepsilon_g:g^{-1}Rg_*\to\mathrm{id}$, are those of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Under these isomorphisms, the $R$-comparison adjoint to $1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_g$ equals $U_{X'}$ of the $k$-comparison adjoint to the same counit formula. On ordinary tensor representatives the coefficient identification is $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\otimes y$.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, prime-torsion reduction and coefficient identity

proof.text:
For any scheme $V$, any $R$-module sheaf $M$ on $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, and any $k$-module sheaf $N$, put $\bar M=M/\ell M$. The sheaf tensor construction gives inverse maps
$$\phi_{M,N}:M\otimes_R U_VN\longrightarrow U_V(\bar M\otimes_kN),\quad x\otimes y\longmapsto\bar x\otimes y,$$
$$\bar x\otimes y\longmapsto x\otimes y.$$
For the inverse, a local lift of $\bar x$ exists because $M\to\bar M$ is a sheaf quotient. Two lifts differ locally by $\ell z$, and $\ell z\otimes y=z\otimes\ell y=0$. Local lifts of a $k$-scalar to $R$ give the balancing identity $ax\otimes y=x\otimes ay$; different lifts differ by a multiple of $\ell$. Thus the rules agree on overlaps and define maps of the sheafified tensors. Both composites fix pure tensors and hence are the identity, by the sheafification universal property. They commute with restrictions and with maps in both $M$ and $N$, since both naturality composites send $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the images of $\bar x$ and $y$. This is an elementary quotient/balancing calculation; it does not assume that $M(U)/\ell M(U)=\bar M(U)$.

source.place: Section Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification and bilinear universal property; elementary quotient calculation expanding the coefficient identity of Tag 0F1J

proof.text: Restriction of scalars is exact: its underlying abelian sheaf, kernels, and sheafified cokernels are unchanged, by the module-sheaf forgetful lemma. Hence it preserves short exact sequences and reflects their exactness. For a short exact sequence of $k$-module sheaves, apply this restriction and tensor with the given flat $R$-module sheaf $\mathcal E$. This sequence remains exact by the definition of sheaf flatness. The natural maps $\phi_{\mathcal E,N}$ of Step 1 identify it with restriction of the sequence obtained by tensoring with $\overline{\mathcal E}$. Exactness is reflected back to $k$-sheaves, so $\overline{\mathcal E}$ is flat. This proves the flatness clause without any flatness assumption on $R\to k$.

source.place: Definition of flat sheaves and elementary application of the quotient tensor identity to exact sequences

proof.text: For $u=p$ and for $u=p\circ h$, apply flat pullback for ringed topoi with constant ring $R$. These are morphisms of topoi by the exactness of the etale inverse image on sheaves of sets. The constant-coefficient module inverse-image lemma identifies $u^*$ with $u^{-1}$, and states its exactness. Consequently $A=p^{-1}\mathcal E$ and $A_Y=h^{-1}A$ are flat. The same argument over $k$, using Step 2, gives flatness of $\bar A=p^{-1}\overline{\mathcal E}$ and $\bar A_Y=h^{-1}\bar A$. Exactness identifies $\bar A=A/\ell A$ and $\bar A_Y=A_Y/\ell A_Y$: apply $u^{-1}$ to the cokernel presentation $\mathcal E\xrightarrow{\ell}\mathcal E\to\overline{\mathcal E}\to0$. These identifications take the quotient map to the quotient map, so their pure-tensor formulas agree with Step 1. The geometric or coefficient flatness of the morphisms $p,h$ is not required.

source.place: Tag 05VD (lemma-pullback-flat); applied to the constant rings and the inverse images in the coefficient identity

proof.text:
For any flat $R$-module sheaf $M$ occurring above, $M[0]$ is K-flat by clause (1) of the K-flat criterion, and its quotient $\bar M[0]$ is K-flat over $k$ by Steps 2--3 and the same criterion. Thus the derived tensor definition computes $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U_VC$ and $\bar M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}C$ by their ordinary termwise tensors for any complex $C$ of $k$-sheaves. Apply $\phi_{M,C^q}$ in each degree. Since the first factor has degree zero, its tensor differential is $1\otimes d_C$, and naturality in Step 1 gives
$$\phi_{M,C^{q+1}}(x\otimes d_Cy)=\bar x\otimes d_Cy=(1\otimes d_C)\phi_{M,C^q}(x\otimes y).$$
The inverse maps also commute with the differential. Localizing this chain isomorphism gives
$$\Phi_{M,C}:M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}U_VC\xrightarrow{\sim}U_V(\bar M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}C).$$
It is natural for derived morphisms of $C$: chain-map naturality was proved above, both sides preserve quasi-isomorphisms because their flat degree-zero first factors are K-flat, and naturality for a roof follows by inverting its quasi-isomorphism. For bounded-below $C$ all these termwise tensors remain bounded below. No degreewise annihilation assertion is made about an independently chosen $R$-injective resolution.

source.place: Tag 06YQ (lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat), Tag 06YU (definition-derived-tor); coefficient identity of Tag 0F1J

proof.text:
Write $G=Rg_{*,k}\mathcal F\in D^+(S'_{\mathrm{et}},k)$. The canonical scalar-restriction comparison, first for $g$ and then for $(f')^{-1}$, gives
$$v:(f')^{-1}Rg_{*,R}U_T\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{X'}(f')^{-1}G.$$
Choose a bounded-below $k$-complex representing $G$; exact derived inverse image computes $(f')^{-1}G$ termwise. Apply Step 4 to $M=A$ and $C=(f')^{-1}G$ after tensoring $v$ with $A$. The resulting map
$$a:A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_{*,R}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{X'}\bigl(\bar A\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}G\bigr)$$
is the first asserted isomorphism (the notation on the left suppresses $U_T$). All direct-image comparisons are used on bounded-below inputs, as required by their statement. This argument uses a $k$-coefficient model through the comparison $v$, rather than asserting that every $R$-coefficient model is degreewise killed by $\ell$.

source.place: Tag 0D6J(3) (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded), Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree); canonical bounded-below coefficient comparison

proof.text:
On $Y$ the inverse-image coefficient comparison identifies $e_R^{-1}U_T\mathcal F$ with $U_Ye_k^{-1}\mathcal F$. Step 4 with $M=A_Y$ gives
$$t:B_R:=A_Y\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e_R^{-1}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YB_k,\qquad B_k:=\bar A_Y\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}e_k^{-1}\mathcal F.$$
These objects are represented by sheaves in degree zero, so are bounded below. Apply $Rh_{*,R}$ to $t$ and then the canonical scalar-restriction direct-image comparison for $h$. Their composite
$$b:Rh_{*,R}B_R\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{X'}Rh_{*,k}B_k$$
is the second asserted isomorphism. Naturality follows from that of $\Phi$, the inverse-image comparison, and the direct-image comparison.

source.place: Tag 0D6J(3) (lemma-modules-abelian-unbounded); the other term in the coefficient reduction of Tag 0F1J

proof.text:
Put $L_R=A\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_{*,R}\mathcal F$ and $L_k=\bar A\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}G$. The tensor and composition comparisons identify
$$h_R^{-1}L_R\cong A_Y\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}e_R^{-1}g_R^{-1}Rg_{*,R}\mathcal F.$$
Here $h^{-1}(f')^{-1}\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}$ uses the equality $f'h=ge$ and the adjunction-compatible inverse-image composition. The defining adjoint map is
$$\alpha_R=1\otimes e_R^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,R}:h_R^{-1}L_R\longrightarrow B_R,$$
and similarly $\alpha_k:h_k^{-1}L_k\to B_k$. Let $c_h:h_R^{-1}U_{X'}L_k\xrightarrow{\sim}U_Yh_k^{-1}L_k$ be the scalar inverse-image comparison. The counit identity for $g$ in the scalar-restriction adjunction lemma, pulled back by $e^{-1}$, together with derived naturality of $\Phi$ from Step 4 gives the equation
$$t\circ\alpha_R=U_Y(\alpha_k)\circ c_h\circ h_R^{-1}(a).$$
Indeed the first tensor factor on both sides is the quotient $A_Y\to\bar A_Y$, and the second factor is the counit identified by that lemma. The tensor and inverse-image composition maps respect these quotient maps by their naturality, so they introduce no further factor in this equation.

source.place: Tag 07A7 (remark-base-change), with Tag 03CB for site composition; definition of the counit adjoint in Tag 0F1J

proof.text:
Let $\kappa_R:L_R\to Rh_{*,R}B_R$ and $\kappa_k:L_k\to Rh_{*,k}B_k$ be the two comparisons. By the adjunction formula, $\kappa_R=Rh_{*,R}(\alpha_R)\circ\eta_{h,R,L_R}$. Substitute Step 7 in this formula, and use naturality of the direct-image scalar comparison $V_h:Rh_{*,R}U_Y\cong U_{X'}Rh_{*,k}$. The unit identity for $h$ in the scalar-restriction adjunction lemma is exactly
$$V_h(h_k^{-1}L_k)\circ Rh_{*,R}(c_h)\circ\eta_{h,R,U_{X'}L_k}=U_{X'}(\eta_{h,k,L_k}).$$
Naturality of the unit with respect to $a$ now gives
$$b\circ\kappa_R=U_{X'}Rh_{*,k}(\alpha_k)\circ U_{X'}(\eta_{h,k,L_k})\circ a=U_{X'}(\kappa_k)\circ a.$$
This is the claimed equality under the displayed source and target isomorphisms. It is an equation obtained from units and counits, and does not require restriction on derived categories to be full or faithful. All tensor identifications have the ordinary representative formula $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\otimes y$ of Step 1.

tool_uses.why: Exactness and reflection of exactness on underlying abelian sheaves justify exact scalar restriction in the elementary quotient-flatness argument.

S3: pullback of flat sheaves along p and ph uses flat-module-pullback with c iso and u^*=u^{-1} (prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact (1)-(3)); the topos morphism comes from the sets inverse-image lemma. Edge cases: n=l (trivial); n=l^2 with E=R (consistent), where E=k non-flat shows the flatness hypothesis is needed; E=0, F=0, n=1 (vacuous).
